hrv_time.note: PRV not ECG-HRV; RMSSD/pNN50 are quantization-sensitive at 1 Hz — lead with SDNN/SDANN

irregular.note: irregular-rhythm SCREEN (not a diagnosis): Poincaré SD1/SD2 + pNN70. PRV not ECG — wrist pulse misses P-waves. Discuss with a clinician only if you have symptoms.

irregular_24h.note: irregular-rhythm SCREEN (not a diagnosis): Poincaré SD1/SD2 + pNN70. PRV not ECG — wrist pulse misses P-waves. Discuss with a clinician only if you have symptoms.

brv.note: Breathing-rate variability TREND (within-user only); surface a change only beyond the metric MDC

rmssd_sleep_session.note: sleep-session HRV: mean RMSSD over cleaned 5-min windows.

rmssd_nocturnal.note: robust nocturnal RMSSD = MEDIAN of 47 consecutive 5-min-window RMSSDs (REM/arousal-robust). PRV not ECG-HRV; RMSSD is quantization-sensitive at 1 Hz.

hrv_freq.note: PRV spectrum; HF band quantization-limited at 1 Hz

resting_hr.note: lowest-30-min mean + 1st-percentile; HR=0 excluded as off-skin

hr_dip.note: night-day HR ratio; CV-risk + acute-strain signal

prsa_dc.note: Bauer 2006 PRSA DC; needs a long overnight RR record for mortality-grade stability

prsa_ac.note: Bauer 2006 PRSA AC; needs a long overnight RR record for mortality-grade stability

cycles_metric.note: need ≥1 h sleep window with sufficient RR for cycle detection

rsa.note: RSA HF-peak respiratory rate (Lomb-Scargle on native beat times, median of 93 300.0s sub-windows, 93 of them within 2.0 br/min of it — brpm, peak_hz and power all come from the medoid sub-window); PRV-derived; this window could resolve up to 30.0 br/min

cvhr_apnea.note: CVHR/ACAT (Hayano) apnea SCREEN — NOT a diagnosis, NOT an AHI; single-night CVHR has substantial night-to-night variability, interpret as a trend over multiple nights

odi.note: refused: the red and IR channels are one signal — ir − red is a fixed offset within a session, so any ratio built from them measures baseline drift, not oxygenation

hrv_night_shape.note: per-bin RMSSD (30-min bins, PRV not ECG-HRV) — a DESCRIPTION of the night, never a cause. A low first third is equally consistent with alcohol, a late meal, late training, a warm room, illness onset, or nothing. Render each bin as a band, not a point.

skin_temp.note: relative deviation (z) vs your baseline; raw sensor units, never an absolute °C

stress.note: Baevsky Stress Index → 0–100; resting autonomic tension (PRV).

spo2.note: refused: the red and IR channels are one signal — ir − red is a fixed offset within a session, so any ratio built from them measures baseline drift, not oxygenation
